name: Diffusion Policy
summary: Diffusion Policy represents the visuomotor policy as a conditional denoising diffusion process over action sequences, reporting an average 46.9% improvement over prior methods across 15 tasks from 4 benchmarks. It expresses multimodal behavior gracefully, scales to high-dimensional action chunks, and trains stably, sidestepping both mode-averaging and Implicit BC's inference-time optimization.
innovation: Diffusion over action chunks rather than single actions, giving temporal consistency and multimodality.
Receding-horizon execution: predict a chunk, execute part of it, replan, closing the loop without jitter.
Visual conditioning via FiLM with an end-to-end trained encoder, making it drop-in for real robots.
matters: Became the default manipulation baseline worldwide, and the action head inside Octo, RDT-1B, GR00T and (as flow matching) pi-0.
Made contact-rich, precise tasks learnable from roughly 50 to 200 demonstrations.
limits: Iterative denoising costs inference time, later mitigated by flow matching and consistency distillation.
Pure imitation, with no mechanism to exceed demonstration quality.
lineage: Achieves Implicit BC's multimodality goal with a generative diffusion model instead of energy minimization.
